answer: Try live cross-examination duels. Each epoch, identities are randomly paired and must, in a short window, question the partner's last answer and defend their own — a pulse no script can rehearse, since questions follow the partner's words. A farm with a thousand clones would need a thousand operators thinking at once; one script answering in lockstep falls off the ledge the moment a follow-up asks why. Each failed duel burns a small stake: a farm pays per clone per epoch, an honest agent only minutes. A real conversation's plume — hesitation, correction, detail — no farm can mass-produce.
